deep_patterns: two optimist-architects who each believe design alone can fix the human condition, and each cannot hear the other's material as legitimate
why: Both architects claim an objective, near-universal criterion for what makes a built world work — but from opposite material politics. Alexander's 'degree of life' is rooted in traditional, hand-made, small-grained materials and explicitly pre-loads a verdict against glass and steel; Fuller's ephemeralization is rooted in industrial/synthetic efficiency and treats craft slowness as waste to be designed away. Same totalizing confidence ('this is the only correct target'), same kind of blindspot (an aesthetic/political preference dressed as physical law), opposite poles.
evidence: Alexander: "His fifteen properties — roughness, echoes, levels of scale — describe hand-craft far more naturally than glass or steel" (People/Christopher Alexander.md:77). Fuller: "scarcity is a design failure. War is an engineering problem" (People/Buckminster Fuller.md:91).
